# Midway M90 Chin Turret
The Midway's fixed twin 90mm turret is operated from its dedicated gunnery seat and console. It supports landed physical fire and delayed flare-assisted impacts during active CAS flybys. Ordinary transit, tactical hover, and takeoff do not support M90 gunnery.
## Setup and Controls - While landed, calibrate the hardpoint with a screwdriver, then use a multitool to program your faction IFF. - Buckle into the gunnery seat and take turret control. Mouse movement aims; hold left click to fire. - The turret slews at sixty degrees per second. WASD or the panel arrows pan its camera; the center button recenters. - All landed fire has a 225-degree forward arc and a twenty-tile maximum range. Rounds stop at the cursor; out-of-range shots are rejected. - Normal and Night optics respect opaque walls. Thermal can observe through walls, but physical shells cannot pass through them. - Mark a target or acquire the current priority hostile, then authorize tracked fire for thirty seconds. Marking alone never permits fire. - AR mode shows the turret's targeting boundary in the main view. Return to the gun panel to leave AR.
## Ammunition and Heat - Load crates with a power loader while landed. Feeds one and two accept any M90 crate; feed three is reserved for Squall. - Select a feed or alternate after each shell. Empty feeds automatically fall back to another loaded feed. - Squall costs 1000 points, contains 1200 kinetic rounds, deals 20 piercing damage per round, and fires ten rounds per second without ejecting casings. It can mark only living targets. - Squall is the only ground-compatible ammunition. HEAP contains 400 explosive rounds and is available during active CAS flybys. - Gale scatter, Ember incendiary, and Tempest devastator are airborne-only explosive feeds. Explosive ammunition fires three shells per second. - Explosive shells heat the barrels faster than Squall. At maximum heat the turret locks until it cools to forty percent. - A feed warns its gunner when it falls below one quarter of its full crate capacity.
## Airborne Flare Fire - Select an active faction signal flare on the right TARGET monitor. Aim within ten tiles of it. - Each shell consumes one round immediately and impacts after a three-second delay, with a visible marker during the final second. - Protected overhead cover, incompatible ammunition, and friendly clearance can prevent a shot. - Friendly clearance is checked again at impact. A cancelled delayed impact does not refund its shell. - Clearing or losing the flare stops airborne fire. Nearby players receive a warning when a gunner locks their flare.
## AI Free Fire and IFF - Enable AI scanning explicitly. Groundside AI fires only after landing on the planet and approving its current target. Approval lasts thirty seconds and requires the gunner to stay seated with the console open. Renew approval after expiry or a target change. - Airborne AI scans active flares and compatible feeds, but each new target requires individual gunner approval. - AI cannot acquire or shoot through walls, even with Thermal selected. - Taking manual control pauses AI scanning without disabling it. Disabling AI starts a five-minute reactivation cooldown. - Groundside AI forces IFF on until close self-defense or an overwhelming group returns control to the gunner's toggle. - Disabling IFF removes friendly shot and impact protection.
## Damage and Rebuilding All xenomorph tiers can damage the exposed mount. The mount has 2000 integrity and disables at zero. Land before beginning a staged engineer rebuild: - Strip the damaged mechanism with a wrench. - Install one box of 90mm repair parts from the dropship fabricator. - Add ten lengths of cable. - Weld the housing with a lit blowtorch, consuming five fuel. - Calibrate and close it with a screwdriver. Interrupted steps do not advance the repair. A completed rebuild restores full integrity.
